title: Awakening a Fundamental Attunement; the First Naming of Profound Boredom (§§16-18)

sections.title: Coming to a preliminary understanding about the significance of awakening a fundamental attunement
Awakening: not ascertaining something at hand, but letting what is asleep become wakeful
The being-there and not-being-there of attunement cannot be grasped via the distinction between consciousness and unconsciousness

key_terms.gloss: awakening; letting what is asleep become wakeful, as opposed to 'ascertaining' (Feststellen) something present-at-hand
ascertaining / fixing-in-place; the objectifying mode that, applied to attunement, destroys or weakens rather than awakens it
attunement / mood; not an interior feeling-state but a disclosive way of being-there, the 'medium' of thinking and acting
fundamental attunement; the originary, pervasive way Dasein is attuned in its very grounds, that which gives Dasein subsistence and possibility
being-there; the name for the being of man, in distinction to the present-at-hand being of the stone
being-away / being absent; an essential way of Dasein's being-there, not non-being; possible only because and so long as man is there
way / manner, but also (literarily) tune or melody; attunement is a Weise that sets the tone for and determines man's being
profound boredom; named here for the first time as the concealed fundamental attunement of the contemporary situation, drawing 'like a silent fog in the abysses of Dasein'
diagnosis / prognosis; foreign words deliberately chosen to mark the non-binding, literary, sensational character of culture-philosophy
setting-out / ascertaining; what philosophy of culture attains (man as expression) instead of his Da-sein, which it is of necessity unable to attain
akinesia (akinesia), motionlessness; Aristotle's characterization of sleep, not tied to (un)consciousness
desmos, a binding / being-bound; Aristotle's account of sleep as a peculiar way in which aisthesis (perception) is bound
aisthesis, perception; what is 'bound' in sleep, so that the ensouled being cannot take in other beings
Nietzsche's fundamental opposition (urge-for-unity vs. urge-for-individuation), named as the common source behind all four cultural diagnoses

claims.text: A fundamental attunement cannot be objectively ascertained (Feststellen); all ascertaining means bringing to consciousness, and with respect to attunement making conscious destroys, weakens, or alters it. The task is therefore to awaken (Wecken) the attunement, i.e., to let what is asleep become wakeful and let it be.

The simultaneous being-there and not-being-there of attunement cannot be grasped through the distinction conscious/unconscious; waking and sleeping are not equivalent to consciousness and unconsciousness, since an animated consciousness (dreaming) pertains to sleep.

The 'there and not there' of attunement belongs to the innermost essence of man's being as Da-sein. Being-away (Weg-sein) is itself a way of man's being and presupposes being-there: man must be-there in order to be able to be away; the stone, in its being away, is precisely not there.

Against the psychological view that ranks feeling third behind thinking and willing as the most inconstant class of lived experience, attunement is a fundamental way of Dasein. It is not inside the soul nor outside; it imposes itself on everything as the medium and presupposition within which thinking and acting first happen.

Because attunement leads back into the grounds of our Dasein, its essence remains concealed; the least-noticed attunements (those in which we seem not attuned at all) are the most powerful. Dasein as Dasein is always already attuned; there is only ever a change of attunement.

Awakening an attunement is a manner of grasping Da-sein as Da-sein, or better, of letting Da-sein be as it is or can be as Da-sein; since this awakening is an acting, we must act in accordance with it rather than merely deliberate about it.
Four contemporary interpretations of our situation (Spengler, Klages, Scheler, Ziegler) share one fundamental trait: they read the situation through the opposition of life (soul) and spirit.
All four interpretations point back to a common source: Nietzsche's fundamental opposition of the Dionysian and the Apollonian; the confrontation proper must occur where this source lies.

The philosophy of culture does not grasp us in our situation but unties us from ourselves by imparting a world-historical role; it offers diagnosis and prognosis that are non-binding, sensational, and literary, illusorily appeasing us.

What lies concealed behind our needing a role, finding no essential possibility of being, and an indifference yawning at us out of all things, is profound boredom (tiefe Langeweile), which draws back and forth like a silent fog in the abysses of Dasein. This is the first naming of profound boredom as the sought-after fundamental attunement to be awakened.

We do not need diagnoses or prognoses of culture to make sure of our situation; rather we must find ourselves by binding ourselves to our Da-sein and letting it become what is singularly binding for us, given over to the task of becoming what we are.

interlocutors.name: Aristotle
interlocutors.role: Ancient authority on sleep: De Somno characterizes sleep as akinesia and as desmos (a binding of aisthesis), grasping it more elementarily than modern misinterpretations; not via (un)consciousness

interlocutors.name: Oswald Spengler
interlocutors.role: First cultural diagnosis ('decline of the West'): the decline of life in and through spirit (ratio); Der Untergang des Abendlandes

interlocutors.name: Ludwig Klages
interlocutors.role: Second diagnosis: spirit as the adversary of the soul, a sickness to be exorcised so life (drives, the mythical) may be liberated; Der Geist als Widersacher der Seele

interlocutors.name: Max Scheler
interlocutors.role: Third diagnosis: a balance between life and spirit ('Man in the epoch of balance' / Der Mensch im Weltalter des Ausgleichs)

interlocutors.name: Leopold Ziegler
interlocutors.role: Fourth (least original) diagnosis: a mediating epoch, a 'new Middle Ages' sublating the opposition of life and spirit; Der europaeische Geist

interlocutors.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
interlocutors.role: The common source of all four diagnoses: the Dionysian/Apollonian opposition (from The Will to Power), driving and transformed across his philosophizing; 'Dionysos versus the Crucified'
